audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart handed Akali levels 3, 4-5, first item and two items, while the whys[] beside it said the opposite ("Level 3 your E gap-close punishes her", "Level 4-5 you keep the trade lead", "Late game your tankier decoy kit out-values her").
audit.why: Akali has no dash until Shuriken Flip at level 3 and it is 16s at rank 1; Wukong out-stats a squishy melee through the early levels. Her one clean window is level 6, when Perfect Execution gives two dashes and an execute. The packet chart and the 52.45% win rate both agree with the whys text, not with the sides.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Wukong / Wukong / Wukong / Wukong / Akali / Skill / Wukong in BOTH layers as matched pairs.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown appeared anywhere in the spike text — her level 6 spike and her shroud reset were both described without numbers.
audit.why: Perfect Execution is 120/90/60s, so the rank-1 window is punishing to waste and long to wait out; Twilight Shroud is 20/19/18/17/16s, which is what actually paces every trade after 3.
audit.corrected: 120s Perfect Execution written into spikes[1].text, 20s Twilight Shroud into phases[5].why, and Shuriken Flip's 16s into phases[2].why.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[1] said shroud is used to 'break your target lock', and the build advice told you to itemize armour against Akali.
audit.why: Twilight Shroud makes Akali invisible AND unable to be selected by enemy spells — Nimbus Strike is a targeted dash, so the shroud denies the engage outright rather than merely dropping a lock. And Akali's damage is magic; armour does nothing, which is why the entry's own boots line already says Mercury's Treads.
audit.corrected: wants.foe[1] restated as denying Nimbus Strike's targeting; armour swapped for magic resist in spikes[3].text and late.

notes: The armour advice was actively harmful here — Akali deals magic damage and the same entry already recommends Mercury's Treads, so the two lines contradicted each other. The decisive interaction is that Twilight Shroud makes her unselectable by spells, which denies Nimbus Strike's target lock entirely; that is now stated on both the wants line and in the mirror's terms.
